data.result:
8 layer(s):
- aspect_deg [continuous, 2 m] Aspect (downslope direction): Direction the ground faces, i.e. the compass bearing of steepest DESCENT, degrees clockwise from north (0 = faces north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west), Horn 3x3 finite difference on the 2 m elevation (about 6 m support), same gradient as slope_2m. 'North-facing' means aspect_deg within 45 deg of 0 (or aspect_class N / NE / NW).
- curvature_plan [continuous, 2 m] Plan curvature (smoothed): Curvature of the contour line across the slope (spurs / ridges diverge = positive, gullies / hollows converge = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. (Zevenbergen and Thorne's raw plan-curvature formula has the opposite sign to their profile formula; plan is flipped here so both read the same way.) 
- curvature_profile [continuous, 2 m] Profile curvature (smoothed): Curvature of the surface along the downslope direction (convex breaks of slope at the top of scarps = positive, concave bases = negative), Zevenbergen and Thorne 3x3 partial-quartic, computed on the elevation after Gaussian smoothing (sigma 5 m = 2.5 cells, kernel truncated at 3 sigma = 15 m radius, full width at half maximum about 12 m) to remove 1-2 m stereo noise; features narrower than roughly 10-15 m are suppressed. Sign convention (both layers): POSITIVE = convex (crest, spur, dome), NEGATIVE = concave (hollow, valley, bowl); values are 1/m, so a paraboloid z = a r^2 gives -2a. (Zevenbergen and Thorne's raw plan-curvature formula has the opposite sign to their profile formula; plan is flipped here so both read the same way.) 
- outcrop_exposure [continuous, 2 m] Outcrop exposure (steep-face relief): Height proxy for an exposed vertical section: local_relief_50m where at least 2% of the cells within 50 m have slope_2m >= 25 degrees (a steep face is actually present in the window), else 0. High values mean tall steep walls nearby, the places where stratigraphy can be seen in section.
- rough_5x5 [continuous, 2 m] Roughness (5x5 elevation std): Standard deviation of elevation in a 5x5 cell (10 m) window, no plane removal, so on tilted ground it includes the slope contribution.
- slope_2m [continuous, 2 m] Slope over 2 m grid (Horn): Surface slope from the 2 m elevation, Horn 3x3 finite difference (about 6 m support).
- tpi_50m [continuous, 2 m] Topographic position index (50 m disc): Cell elevation minus the mean elevation of the other cells within 50 m (disc, centre excluded) on the 2 m grid. Positive = above its surroundings (ridge, crest, mesa top), negative = below (hollow, channel, crater floor next to a rim), about 0 = flat or mid-slope.
- tri [continuous, 2 m] Terrain ruggedness index (3x3): Riley et al. ruggedness: square root of the summed squared elevation differences between a cell and its 8 neighbours (2 m cells, 6 m window). Unit is metres; includes the slope contribution (a smooth 30 deg ramp has a high TRI).
Next: describe_layer(id) for limits, quality and citation before relying on a layer.
